summary.short: Creates powers for customer and business data access regulations (Part 1), a trust framework and register for digital verification services (Part 2), a national underground asset register (Part 3), changes to registers of births and deaths (Part 4), and UK GDPR and privacy amendments (Part 5).
summary.long: The text provided has five Parts. Part 1 confers powers on the Secretary of State and the Treasury to make regulations requiring data holders to provide customer data and business data to customers or authorised third-party recipients, with supplementary provision on interfaces, decision-makers, enforcement, financial penalties, fees and levies, and review duties. Part 2 requires the Secretary of State to publish a DVS trust framework and maintain a register of digital verification services, with registration tied to certification by accredited conformity assessment bodies, and powers to refuse, remove or amend entries. Part 3 requires a National Underground Asset Register, with duties on undertakers to enter and correct apparatus information and offences for non-compliance. Part 4 changes how registers of births and deaths are kept. Part 5, Chapter 1 amends the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018, including recognised legitimate interests, purpose limitation and consent provisions. The long title also refers to copyright and the development of artificial intelligence systems, but the text provided ends within Part 5 and contains no operative AI or copyright provisions. The outline supplied with the document is empty.

notes: Part 1 of 3 covers sections 1 to 72 and the opening heading of Schedule A1, which is cut off. Schedules 1 to 5, 2ZA, 5A and A1 and the Schedule 3 minor amendments fall outside this part and are not annotated here. Target instruments are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty. Quotes containing footnote markers (for example 'F1Commission') keep the markers as printed. Relations record amendments and repeals as stated in the text; no effects are assessed. Section_status is set to not_applicable only because the schema requires both keys; populated relations and entities are listed above. Part 2 of 3 covers ss. 73 to 144 and the start of Schedule 1; the operative content of Schedule 1 and later Schedules is in part 3. Schedule-level amendments and Ministerial powers to make regulations are coded here only as relations and entities. Drafting inconsistency: s. 101(3) (new Sch. 16 para. 4 A2) refers to 'the Commission' while the surrounding provisions refer to 'the Commissioner'. Commencement per s. 142: ss. 66, 78, 126 to 128 and Part 8 come into force on the day of Royal Assent; ss. 69, 82, 96 and 97 come into force two months later; the rest by regulation under s. 142(1). Relation rows use an empty target_instrument_id where no registry identifier was available; the named instrument is in target_text. Part 3 covers Schedules 1 to 16 only; the excerpt opens mid-Schedule 1 (section 106G), and the Act into which section 106G is inserted is not named in this part. Schedule 2 inserts a Northern Ireland equivalent (Article 45G, Schedule 2ZA) into the Street Works (Northern Ireland) Order 1995. No penalty amount appears in this part; Sch 1 para 1(2) leaves amounts to regulations. Internal variance: the GB penalty provision (Sch 1 para 1(5)) makes regulations subject to the affirmative procedure, but the Northern Ireland text (Sch 2 para 1) has no equivalent subsection; the NI text also reads a county court where the GB text reads the county court. Sch 13 modifies section 155 to refer to the Commission while other provisions in the PEC modification refer to the Commissioner. Commencement is not stated in this part; several Schedules (7, 8, 9, 14) depend on commencement regulations or transitional 'relevant day' provisions. Several provisions cross-refer to sections of this Act or of the 2018 Act outside this part (e.g. sections 106E, 106F, 118, 164A, 165). Registry IDs were not supplied, so all target_instrument_id values are empty.
